Final learned centers

What happened during learning?

  1. Initialize from data. K-means++ selects K starting rows from the CSV.
  2. Assign rows. Every row joins the closest current center.
  3. Recalculate centers. Each center becomes the mean of its assigned rows.
  4. Repeat. Continue until assignments are stable and movement is within tolerance, or the iteration limit is reached.

Several starting attempts reduce sensitivity to initialization. The attempt with the smallest final inertia is selected; a global optimum is not guaranteed.
